title: Shell command timeout does not reap the child process tree; orphans hold cargo locks
wanted_capability: When a shell_run/shell_poll command hits its timeout (or is killed), the harness should terminate the entire process group/tree, not just the direct child. Today a timed-out cargo command leaves sccache/rustc grandchildren alive holding the target-dir build lock; the next cargo command blocks on the lock and the bro burns a multi-turn forensic loop (pgrep/ps/kill cycles) to find and reap the orphans. W7a did this cleanup dance three separate times in one session; each cost 5-10 turns and several minutes.
missing_primitive: process-group spawn (setsid/setpgid) + group kill on timeout/shell_kill
fallback_used: Bros manually pgrep/ps to identify orphaned cargo/rustc/sccache PIDs under their target dir and kill them individually before retrying.
evidence: W7a session faef2ed8 narration: three orphan-cleanup loops after 600s timeouts (PIDs 11254/29258/48211 + compiler children) each holding /Users/invidious/repos/ts-w7a/target lock
resolution_note: Addressed in 5b84b5c (w8, folded to beta, deployed 2026-06-10): shell commands spawn as their own process-group leader (process_group(0)) and every kill path signals the whole group via negative-pid kill(2) — timeout escalation in drive(), signal_child (shell_poll signal= / shell_kill), the overflow rejection path, and a new ShellSession Drop covering abandoned live sessions (kill_on_drop only reaps the direct child). Mirrors codex-rs's killpg-based group cleanup (utils/pty/src/process_group.rs). Regression test timeout_kills_backgrounded_grandchildren proves a timed-out command's backgrounded children die with the group. A timed-out cargo no longer leaves sccache/rustc holding the target-dir lock.
